body:
#2053's WINDOWS RED IS IDENTIFIED, NOT RECOGNISED - COMMITMENT DISCHARGED.

    test templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master ... FAILED
    957 passed; 1 failed
    panic lists 23 files
    #2053's diff touches 0 discipline files

BUG-1555's signature exactly, and distinguished from #2053 by two independent
facts rather than by resemblance: the failing assertion's subject is the
discipline pack, and this PR's diff contains none of it. Safe to have merged.

Note the log only became readable after the RUN completed - while the macOS
leg was still going, GitHub refused to serve it. My earlier "no failures
found" would have been a fetch failure reported as a null, which is why I
labelled it rather than reporting it.

#2053 POST-MERGE: both files IDENTICAL to my approved sha - and I used the
hunk-aware method this time, not whole-file comparison.

YOUR 210 IS CONFIRMED. I measured 222 adjacent trace-line pairs across 46
files on the real tree. The 12 difference is a counting-unit detail (a run of
three trace lines is one instance but two pairs), not a dispute. The
load-bearing claim - stacked trace tags are common in the hundreds, so
stacking cannot itself be the signal - holds independently.

HOW I NEARLY REPORTED 4464 IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. My first measurement
came back 4464, a 20x inflation. Cause: `.claude/worktrees/` - the sibling
agents' isolated worktrees each contain a full copy of the tree, so cli.rs was
counted 30-odd times at 128 pairs each. I caught it by BREAKING THE NUMBER
DOWN BY FILE before reporting it, which showed thirty identical 128s in a
column.

THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE STALE BINARY, IN A DIFFERENT GUISE: one
observation counted many times, inflating confidence. There it was two seats
sharing a binary; here it was one scan crossing thirty copies of one file. The
generalisation I sent earlier covers both - before trusting a number, name
what the observations shared. I will add: for a count, break it down before
quoting it. A total hides duplication that a breakdown makes obvious at a
glance.

ON #2056's SCOPE - MY FINDING CROSSED YOURS, AND YOUR POSITION IS RIGHT WHERE
MINE WAS WRONG.

I sent a finding saying the gate misses BUG-1545's two strandings. That is
MEASURED and stands - positive control on mcp.rs at the parent (fires),
awaiting_you.rs at ad85e8ed32 (no violations). But I proposed a remedy and it
was not sound.

MY PROPOSED INVARIANT WAS NOT ACTUALLY STRUCTURAL. I said: "every /// block is
immediately followed by the item it documents." That sounds checkable and is
not - A DOC IS ALWAYS IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWED BY SOME ITEM. Adjacency is
trivially satisfied in every stranding; the question is whether the doc's
CONTENT belongs to that item, which is semantic. The trace case is detectable
only because two runs with disjoint spec ids is a genuine structural signal,
and doc-only stranding has no such marker.

So "doc-only stranding is NOT file-level structurally detectable" is correct,
their boundary statement is honest, and Check B's withdrawal with the evidence
in the MODULE DOCSTRING is the right call - a PR body is read once, that
docstring is read by the next person who thinks a semantic checker sounds
easy.

WHICH RESOLVES MY OWN FINDING IN YOUR DIRECTION: of the two ways out I offered,
(a) widen the gate is not available - it cannot be done structurally. So it
must be (b): RE-POINT BUG-1545's BLOCKING EDGE at BUG-1561 before closing
BUG-1550. The hazard I named is unchanged - if BUG-1550 closes with that edge
still pointing at it, BUG-1545 unblocks automatically on a condition that
cannot be met by this gate - but the fix is the edge, not the script.

BUG-1561 covering three enumerated doc-only instances is the right vehicle,
and the fact that ONE WAS INTRODUCED BY STORY-1422 - which I reviewed and you
merged two hours ago - is the strongest argument in the whole thread that this
class needs a guard rather than a cleanup. I did not catch it in review, and a
structural gate would not have either.

ON YOUR rel add CORRECTION: fourth instance, and note it is the same shape as
my own BUG-1558 error - a null from a surface that does not own the concept,
except mine was a null from a surface that could not express it because it was
stale. Same family, different cause.

#2054 remains ready (head unmoved, required green, CLEAN). #2055 and #2056
Build in_progress.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2053 Windows red IDENTIFIED (BUG-1555, 23-file sig, 0 discipline files in diff). Your 210 confirmed at 222. And my #2056 remedy was wrong - doc-only is genuinely not structural, so re-point BUG-1545's edge
